adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member in groups_controller.rb passes a raw Integer id into group.users.delete(user_id), which may raise or silently succeed without removing anything, and returns success even for nonexistent user_id

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` where `user_id` is an integer. In Rails/ActiveRecord, `has_many`/`has_and_belongs_to_many` association `delete` accepts ids as well as records, so the claim that passing an Integer "may raise" is not supported by the diff. The fact it returns success even if the id isn’t a member is an idempotent/no-op delete behavior and is consistent with prior code paths (membership removals previously also succeeded silently when the target user wasn’t effectively removed), so it’s not a verifiable defect from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group members route/template mismatch: route sets model to the group object while template iterates {{#each m in members}}, which only works if the controller proxies properties; otherwise public group members page renders empty

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the group-members route now sets the controller `model` to the Group object and calls `model.findMembers()`. In `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, the AJAX response populates `members` on the group via `self.setProperties({ ..., members: ... })`. The template was updated from iterating `model` to iterating `members`, which is consistent with storing members on the group model. The finding’s claim that this “only works if the controller proxies properties” is speculative; the diff itself shows `members` is now a property on the model being set, so there is no verifiable mismatch introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec tests use xhr :put for remove_member but the route is defined as delete, so the tests route to add_members and never exercise remove_member
addMembers/removeMember AJAX calls in group.js model have no .catch/error handler, so failures are silent and the promise isn't returned to the controller for handling

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, both `removeMember` and `addMembers` explicitly `return Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)`, so the promise *is* returned from the model methods. The controller actions (`removeMember`/`addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6`) also don’t return those promises, but that’s separate from the finding’s claim about the model. While there’s no explicit `.catch` handler shown, the diff alone doesn’t prove failures are “silent” (Discourse.ajax may have global error handling).

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames input is never cleared after successful add in admin-group.js.es6 addMembers action, allowing duplicate re-submission

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the new `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.get("usernames")` after `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));`, so the UI will keep the previous usernames and allows repeated submissions. The diff does not show this causing incorrect server-side state (duplicates may be ignored), but it is a concrete UX/behavior issue grounded in the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise on the empty-name path, which will crash callers that chain .then()
N+1 query shape in add_members: one SELECT per username plus individual group_user inserts (~2N queries) instead of a single User.where bulk lookup plus bulk insert

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames.split(",").each do |username|; if user = User.find_by_username(username); group.add(user); end; end` which performs one user lookup query per username (N SELECTs). Additionally, `group.add(user)` will typically create a membership row per user (N inserts), yielding ~2N DB operations instead of a bulk `User.where(username: ...)` lookup and bulk association insert. This is a concrete performance/query-shape issue introduced by the diff, not a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No cap on the size of the usernames param in add_members, allowing clients to submit thousands of names and produce an unbounded loop of queries in one request

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff adds `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and performs `User.find_by_username(username)` inside the loop. There is no cap/validation on the length or number of comma-separated usernames, so a client can submit a very large list and trigger an unbounded number of DB lookups/add operations in a single request (potential DoS/performance issue).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No upper bound/clamp on limit in the public groups members endpoint, allowing ?limit=10000000 to materialize and serialize entire huge group memberships

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination uses `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then applies `.limit(limit)` without any upper bound or clamping. This allows requests like `?limit=10000000` to trigger fetching/serializing an extremely large number of members (`group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`), which is a plausible DoS/performance issue on this public endpoint (guarded only by `ensure_can_see!`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant COUNT(*) over group_users on every members page fetch, even though a cheap cached user_count counter (used in BasicGroupSerializer) exists

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` and returns it in `meta.total` on every members fetch (now paginated). This performs a COUNT over the group users association each request, even though the `Group` model/serializer already exposes a `user_count` counter (used elsewhere via `BasicGroupSerializer`). This is a real performance/architecture concern grounded in the new code, but not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Off-by-one in totalPages: uses Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 instead of Math.ceil, producing an empty phantom page that triggers a wasted fetch when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
Client-side offset clamp in findMembers uses stale user_count computed before the fetch, causing non-limit-aligned offsets and unstable pagination math with redundant refetches

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` the request offset is clamped using the *current* client-side `user_count` **before** the AJAX fetch updates it: `var ... offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));` and then `meta.total` is applied after the response. If `user_count` is stale (e.g. after add/remove membership triggers `self.findMembers()`), this clamp can be wrong and the client can request an out-of-range offset and get an empty/incorrect page. Additionally, the pagination actions clamp to `user_count` (`next`: `Math.min(..., group.get("user_count"))`), which can set `offset == user_count` (not limit-aligned) and trigger a fetch for an empty page, reinforcing the pagination instability described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Full member-list reload (findMembers) after every single add/remove member operation, issuing N mutations → N refetches each including COUNT(*)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly triggers a full member-list refetch after each membership mutation: in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers()` and `removeMember()` call `self.findMembers()` in their success callbacks. `findMembers()` hits `/groups/:name/members.json` and the server endpoint `GroupsController#members` computes `total = group.users.count`, so every refetch includes a COUNT(*) query. This is a performance/architecture concern (N mutations cause N refetches + counts), not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking response-shape change to public /groups/:name/members endpoint: previously returned a bare JSON array of serialized users, now returns {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}}, breaking existing consumers (plugins, themes, API clients) with no versioning or compatibility shim (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-31)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` to an explicit `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). That is a response-shape change for the non-admin `/groups/:name(members)` endpoint, and the front-end code was updated accordingly (template now iterates `members` instead of `model`). Any existing consumers expecting the prior top-level serialized user collection would break without a compatibility shim/versioning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Default pagination limit of 50 silently truncates member lists for external consumers: previously non-automatic groups returned all members, now every group defaults to limit: 50 with no error and no signal unless meta is read (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:21)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes the endpoint to always apply pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, whereas previously non-automatic groups returned the full member list (no `limit/offset` unless `group.automatic?`). This is a potentially breaking API behavior change for consumers expecting all members, but the new response also includes a `meta` block with `total/limit/offset`, so it’s not an outright correctness defect—more an API-compatibility/contract concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of PATCH membership path from Admin::GroupsController#update: PATCH requests with changes: {add/delete} now fall into the plain update branch which ignores changes, returning a 200 success with membership changes silently dropped instead of a 410/unsupported error (app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:29-42)

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific handling in `Admin::GroupsController#update` (old `if request.patch? then update_patch(group)` branch is gone) and the new `update` method only updates `alias_level`, `visible`, and (non-automatic) `name` (it never reads `params[:changes]`). Since Rails `resources :groups` still provides a PATCH route, a PATCH request with `changes: {add/delete}` will hit `update`, ignore membership changes, and still attempt `group.save` and return `success_json` on success—silently dropping the requested membership modifications.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes PATCH-specific behavior in `Admin::GroupsController#update` (old `update_patch` branch and related specs under `context 'incremental'` are deleted), and no new spec asserts what happens for PATCH requests now. Separately, `GroupsController#members` changes from `render_serialized(members, ...)` to a new JSON envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (and JS `Group#findMembers` now relies on `result.meta`/`result.members`), but the diff adds no controller spec covering this new public response shape. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap around newly changed behavior/APIs, not a directly verifiable runtime defect within the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined when group name is empty instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]), breaking .then() promise chains for callers like setupController and group-members route

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the guard changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` to `return ;` when `name` is empty. That makes the method return `undefined` in that case, instead of a thenable/promise, which is an API/consistency regression and could break any callers that still do `findMembers().then(...)`. However, in this diff the cited callers (`admin_group_route` and `group-members` route) were changed to call `model.findMembers();` without chaining, so the specific “breaking .then() promise chains for callers like setupController and group-members route” claim isn’t directly verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec uses xhr :put, :remove_member but route is defined as delete "members" => "groups#remove_member", so the spec doesn't exercise the actual route

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb under context ".remove_member", the first test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but config/routes.rb defines the route as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Since controller specs invoke the action directly, this PUT request can still pass even though the real endpoint only accepts DELETE, meaning the spec doesn’t actually exercise the routed behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: In remove_member, group.users.delete(user_id) already destroys the join record immediately, making the subsequent group.save a no-op that can't fail — render_json_error is dead code and DB errors are unhandled

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`. The association deletion is performed immediately by `delete`, so the subsequent `group.save` is likely redundant and often a no-op (no model attributes changed). That makes the error branch very unlikely in normal operation, and it also doesn’t handle exceptions raised by the `delete` itself. However, from the diff alone it’s not provable that `group.save` “can’t fail” (validations/callbacks could still theoretically return false), so calling it a definite bug/dead code is overstated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently ignores nonexistent usernames and still returns success_json, giving the admin no indication which members failed to add

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is added only if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; missing users are simply skipped (`if user = ...; group.add(user); end`). The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, with no reporting of which usernames were invalid. However, the prior codebase explicitly had tests asserting this “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” behavior (now removed), suggesting this is an intentional UX choice rather than a clear correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members/remove_member are not wrapped in an ActiveRecord transaction, so partial failure leaves the group half-updated while still returning success

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `add_members` loops over usernames and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then returns `success_json` only if `group.save` succeeds; otherwise it returns `render_json_error(group)` (same for `remove_member` after `group.users.delete(user_id)`). The finding’s core claim — that partial failure can leave the group half-updated *while still returning success* — is not supported by the shown control flow. Lack of an explicit transaction is visible, but the diff does not show any path where a failure occurs and the controller still returns success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Frontend addMembers/removeMember/findMembers have no .catch/error handlers and no loading/disabled state on buttons, so on failure the admin gets zero feedback and can repeatedly click Add firing duplicate requests

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds async member-management actions (`addMembers`, `removeMember`, pagination `next`/`previous`) that call `group.addMembers(...)`, `group.removeMember(...)`, and `group.findMembers()` which are `Discourse.ajax(...)` calls in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`. These methods/actions only attach `.then(...)` handlers (e.g., reload members) and do not add any `.catch(...)`/failure handling or user-visible error reporting. In the template (`admin/templates/group.hbs` and `group_member.hbs`), the Add button and remove link have no disabled/loading binding, so repeated clicks can fire multiple requests; additionally `addMembers` even has a `// TODO: should clear the input`, confirming no state reset. This is a concrete UX/robustness gap introduced by the change, but not a strictly verifiable correctness break from the diff alone (errors may be handled globally).

adjudication_records.issue_text: setupController in admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6 fires findMembers() without returning the promise, so no loading indicator is set, no error handler exists, and route transition is no longer blocked until data arrives
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that findMembers() is invoked asynchronously without its promise being handled/returned, meaning the route/controller proceeds before member data is available (race condition / transition not blocked). Candidate adds extra consequences (no loading/error handling) but same core issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, causing an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit — showingLast never becomes true and users can page into an empty page

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. As a result `showingLast` (`propertyEqual("currentPage", "totalPages")`) won’t become true on the real last page, and `actions.next` can advance `offset` to `user_count` (e.g., 100). `Group.findMembers` then requests members with `offset: 100`, and `GroupsController#members` applies `.limit(limit).offset(offset)`, returning an empty `members` list. This matches the reported empty-page behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: offset clamp in next (Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)) sets offset to user_count rather than the last full page boundary, producing inconsistent current-page display

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next` action clamps `offset` with `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which allows `offset` to become exactly `user_count`. Since `Group.findMembers` sends that `offset` through to `/groups/:name/members.json`, this can request an empty page (offset at end of dataset). This is especially reachable because `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50 => 3), enabling navigation to the extra empty page where `offset == user_count` and `currentPage` becomes that extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: create/save action in admin-group.js controller may leave disableSave permanently true on promise rejection (e.g., 422 duplicate group name) if no .catch is used

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the `save` action now calls `group.save()` / `group.create()` instead of `saveWithUsernames` / `createWithUsernames`, but it does not show the rest of the `save` action where `disableSave` would be set/reset or where promise rejections are handled. There’s no diff evidence that `disableSave` is left true on rejection (or that `.catch`/failure handling is missing), so the finding can’t be verified from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit param (limit=1000000) allowing a client to dump the entire user list of any visible group in one query — DoS/abuse vector

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the server trusts `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound (`app/controllers/groups_controller.rb`). This allows a client to request an arbitrarily large page size (e.g. `limit=1000000`) and force a huge query/serialization response for any visible group, creating an abuse/DoS vector. The diff specifically introduces/extends this parameterized pagination behavior for all groups without clamping `limit`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers clamps offset against stale client-side user_count before the request, so requested offset can be beyond real data with no server-side clamp, returning an empty list displayed as no members

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, the requested `offset` is clamped using the client-side `user_count` (`Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`). If `user_count` is stale (e.g., members were removed elsewhere since the last fetch), the client can still request an `offset` beyond the real total. The server endpoint `GroupsController#members` applies the provided `offset` directly (`.limit(limit).offset(offset)`) with no clamp against `total = group.users.count`, so an out-of-range offset will return an empty `members` array. This can result in an empty member list being displayed even though the group has members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs references automatic via the item view context chain inside an each member loop; if the context is the member, automatic may be undefined and the remove link shown/hidden incorrectly

adjudication.rationale: In `group.hbs`, members are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and the item view template (`admin/templates/group_member.hbs`) uses `{{#unless automatic}} ... {{/unless}}`. In an `each` item context, `automatic` is likely looked up on the iterated member object (a `Discourse.User` created in `Group.findMembers`), which does not have an `automatic` property, making it `undefined`/falsey and causing the remove link to render even for automatic groups. This would expose a UI control that should be hidden (and would hit server-side `can_not_modify_automatic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public groups#members endpoint response format changed with no request spec coverage at all, breaking plugin consumers silently

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the response changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (an array) to a wrapped object `{ members: ..., meta: ... }` (see `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb` diff). That is an API contract change for the public `/groups/:id/members` endpoint, and this diff does not add any spec coverage for that controller/endpoint (only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is modified). This is a concrete, diff-grounded risk of silently breaking external/plugin consumers, even though the app’s own JS was updated to expect `result.members`/`result.meta`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: limit/offset params on groups#members are not clamped, so negative or huge values pass straight to SQL, and this behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff now always applies pagination from request params: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, and then uses them directly in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation to prevent negative `offset` or excessively large `limit`, so arbitrary values from the client can flow straight into the SQL `LIMIT/OFFSET` (potential SQL error for negative offsets and/or performance/DoS risk for huge limits). The PR also adds no controller spec coverage for this `groups#members` pagination behavior (the updated specs only cover admin group create/update/destroy/add_members/remove_member).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of the old 200-group truncation workaround is unverified by tests

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the previous conditional workaround for automatic groups (default `limit` 200 with `offset` support, with a TODO about truncation) was removed and replaced with unconditional pagination (`limit` default 50, always applies) and a new `meta.total/limit/offset` response. The diff adds/updates tests for `Admin::GroupsController`, but does not add any tests for `GroupsController#members`, so this behavior change (and the removal of the old truncation-related workaround) is not covered by tests in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put but the route declares delete, so the test exercises a request that can never occur in production

adjudication.rationale: In routes.rb, member removal is wired as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, while the spec `context ".remove_member"` has a test that calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`. That PUT would not hit `remove_member` via routing in production (it would align with the PUT members route for `add_members`), so the test is exercising an HTTP method/route combination that won't occur in real usage. This is a test correctness issue, not a production defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No request spec confirms the HTTP verbs for the add_members route (only exists as PUT)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds verb-specific routes under `admin/groups` (`put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` in `config/routes.rb`). The accompanying test coverage is in a controller spec (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`) using `xhr :put, :add_members`, which exercises the controller action but does not verify the routing/HTTP verb mapping itself (i.e., that PUT is wired to `add_members` and other verbs are rejected). So the finding about missing request/routing-level confirmation of the HTTP verb is diff-grounded, but it’s a test gap rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Lost test coverage for silently ignoring non-existent users when adding members; new add_members silent-ignore behavior is untested

adjudication.rationale: The previous spec coverage for silently ignoring non-existent users was removed (old `.update` PATCH context had `it "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users" ...`). The new implementation in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` still silently ignores unknown usernames (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`), but the new `context ".add_members"` tests only cover automatic-group rejection and adding valid users, with no test for unknown usernames. This is a specific, diff-grounded loss of test coverage for that behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that remove_member succeeds silently when removing a non-member

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `remove_member` endpoint (`Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`) that calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then saves, but the updated specs only cover (1) automatic group rejection and (2) removing an existing member. The previous test suite explicitly covered “succeeds silently when removing non-members” under the old incremental PATCH flow, and that coverage was removed. There is no new spec asserting the non-member removal case for the new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination logic totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an extra empty page when user_count % limit == 0

adjudication.rationale: `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 100 users with limit 50), this returns 3 instead of 2, creating an extra empty page. This is exacerbated by `actions.next`, which can set `offset` to `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` will then request `offset=user_count`, yielding an empty member list while `currentPage/totalPages` show the extra page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: currentPage in admin-group.js.es6 has the same off-by-one rounding problem

adjudication.rationale: `currentPage` is computed as `Math.floor(offset/limit) + 1` (admin-group.js.es6). But the pagination actions allow `offset` to reach `user_count` (`next` sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`). When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50), `offset` can become 100, making `currentPage` = 3 even though there are only 2 pages. This is an off-by-one pagination bug exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The findMembers/next/previous pagination state machine (offset clamping, meta round-trip) has no JS tests at all

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial client-side pagination/state logic in `admin-group.js.es6` (`currentPage`, `totalPages`, `showingFirst/Last`, and `actions.next/previous` updating `model.offset` and calling `group.findMembers()`), and changes `Discourse.Group#findMembers` to clamp/round-trip pagination via server `meta` (`limit/offset/total`, setting `members`, `user_count`, etc.). The only tests added/modified are Ruby controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`); there are no JS/QUnit/Ember tests in the diff covering the new pagination state machine behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group creation no longer accepts usernames param but the new create-then-addMembers flow is untested at controller and integration level

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes support for passing usernames during group creation: the client model `Discourse.Group#create()` now POSTs only `asJSON()` (name/alias_level/visible) and `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads top-level `params[:name]` / `params[:visible]` with no `usernames` handling. Membership is now managed via separate endpoints (`add_members` / `remove_member`) and UI action `addMembers`. While there are controller specs for `create` and for `add_members` separately, there is no test that exercises the combined create-then-add-members flow (e.g., create via controller then add_members using the returned id), and no integration/client-level test coverage is shown for this new workflow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test verifies a stale usernames param is harmlessly ignored on create

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, `Admin::GroupsController#create` no longer reads any `usernames` input (it only uses `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]`), so a client sending a stale/extra `usernames` param would currently be ignored. The updated specs under `context ".create"` only verify whitespace stripping on `name` and do not assert that providing `usernames` during create has no effect (e.g., does not add members / does not error). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The render_json_error branch on failed save in Admin::GroupsController#update is never exercised by tests

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the failure branch `else render_json_error group` remains, but the updated spec only covers a successful update (`context ".update"` tests automatic-group name ignoring + visible change) and does not include any case where `group.save` returns false. So the error-handling branch is not exercised by tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: alias_level assignment (including non-numeric input via .to_i) in update is untested

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#update, alias_level is now assigned from `params[:alias_level].to_i` when present (`group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?`). The updated controller spec for `.update` only tests ignoring name changes for automatic groups and setting `visible`, and does not exercise alias_level updates or how non-numeric input is coerced by `.to_i`. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing test for changed parameter handling, but not a proven runtime defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: refresh_automatic_groups test verifies the mock stub was called rather than actual group refresh behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".refresh_automatic_groups"`, the test stubs/sets an expectation `Group.expects(:refresh_automatic_groups!).returns(true)` and only asserts the response is 200 after `xhr :post, :refresh_automatic_groups`. This verifies the mocked method invocation rather than any actual side effects of refreshing automatic groups, so it’s a test quality/coverage concern rather than a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test that user_count stays consistent after add/remove of members, which the frontend pagination depends on; stale count would go uncaught

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces frontend pagination that depends on `user_count` (`currentPage`, `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6`) and updates `user_count` from the `/groups/:name/members.json` response meta in `Discourse.Group#findMembers`. After `addMembers`/`removeMember`, the model reloads via `findMembers()`, so keeping `meta.total`/`user_count` correct is important. The new controller specs for `add_members` and `remove_member` only assert `group.users.count` in the database, and do not assert that the members endpoint returns the correct `meta.total` or that `user_count` used for pagination stays in sync after add/remove. So this is a concrete, diff-grounded missing test for newly added behavior rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers() promise in setupController (admin_group_route.js and group-members.js.es6) is fire-and-forget, so failures (403/404/network errors) are silently swallowed and the UI shows an empty member list with no error indication

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` now calls `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise (`afterModel` hooks that returned the promise were removed). `Discourse.Group#findMembers` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and does not attach error handling. Because this promise is no longer part of the route’s transition promise chain, failures (403/404/network) won’t trigger Ember’s route error handling and the `members` property will never be set, leaving the UI to render an empty list with no error indication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers now mutates the model (sets members, user_count, offset, limit) rather than returning data, leaking paginated member-list view-state into the group domain model

adjudication.rationale: Verified: `Discourse.Group#findMembers` changed from returning an array of members (`then(function(result) { return result.map(...) })`) to mutating the group model via `self.setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members: ... })` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js). The model also gained pagination/view-state fields (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`) at the top of the class. This does mix paginated member-list state into the group domain model, which is an architecture/scope concern, but the diff does not show a clear correctness break by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client totalPages computation floor(user_count / limit) + 1 has an off-by-one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 100 users, limit 50 → empty page 3)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count > 0`). For exact multiples (e.g. 100 users, limit 50), this yields 3 instead of 2. The `next` action also allows `offset` to become exactly `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` then queries with that offset, which will return an empty `members` list. This creates an empty extra page, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination logic duplicated in three places with different semantics (model clamp, controller next/previous, server-echoed meta offset), risking drift; should be extracted into a shared mixin/component

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces pagination state/logic spread across (1) the Ember controller (`currentPage`, `totalPages`, `actions.next/previous` computing/clamping offsets), (2) the client model (`Group.findMembers` clamps `offset` and overwrites `limit/offset/user_count` from `result.meta`), and (3) the server response (`GroupsController#members` computes `limit/offset/total` and echoes them back in `meta`). This is a real maintainability/architecture concern because changes to paging semantics (clamping, last page behavior, etc.) must be kept consistent across these layers, increasing drift risk, but it’s not a concrete, directly verifiable functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member in groups_controller.rb bypasses the model API using group.users.delete(user_id) instead of the domain group.remove method, skipping invariants

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb`, the new `remove_member` action removes membership via `group.users.delete(user_id)` rather than using the higher-level API that the codebase previously used (`group.remove(user)` existed in the removed `update_patch` logic, and `add_members` still uses `group.add(user)`). The diff confirms this is a deliberate bypass of the domain method, which could skip any encapsulated invariants/callbacks in `Group#remove`, but the diff does not prove this causes a concrete correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Asymmetric persistence: add_members calls group.save after only mutating the join table, while remove_member relies on users.delete persisting immediately

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows *both* `add_members` and `remove_member` call `group.save` after mutating membership. In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, it does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `if group.save ...`; it does not “rely on users.delete persisting immediately” without saving. Thus the claimed asymmetry is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames controller property is write-only state never cleared after addMembers (acknowledged by TODO), so stale usernames persist between adds and across group switches

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `usernames` is now a plain controller property (`usernames: null`) rather than being derived from `members`, and `actions.addMembers` explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` but does not clear `this.usernames` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`. Additionally, `AdminGroupRoute.setupController` sets only `model` and calls `model.findMembers()`; it does not reset `controller.usernames`, so if the same controller instance is reused when switching groups, the previous `usernames` value can persist into the next group view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, creating an inconsistent 'may or may not return a promise' contract that will break future callers chaining on the result

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` was changed from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` on empty name to `return ;` (undefined): `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`. This creates an inconsistent return contract (sometimes a promise, sometimes undefined). The diff also shows callers were updated to no longer chain (`afterModel` hooks removed and `model.findMembers();` called without `then`), so it may not break current code shown here, but it is a real API design issue that could trip any caller that does `findMembers().then(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently skips non-existent usernames without any error or partial-success feedback, and the client just reloads members, so the user gets no indication a username was not added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are processed with `usernames.split(",").each` and only added if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; non-existent usernames are simply skipped (`if user = ... group.add(user) end`) and the action still renders `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. On the client side, `Group#addMembers` just reloads the member list via `self.findMembers()` with no way to surface partial failures. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/feedback gap, but not a verifiable correctness defect (the server intentionally treats unknown users as no-ops).

adjudication_records.issue_text: group/members.hbs template iterates a members property that only exists after the async findMembers resolves via fire-and-forget mutation, making the route/controller/template contract implicit and fragile

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the route now does `controller.set("model", model); model.findMembers();` without awaiting a promise, and `group/members.hbs` was changed to iterate `{{#each m in members}}` instead of `model`. The `members` collection is only populated asynchronously via `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, which mutates the group model (`self.setProperties({ members: ... })`). This works, but it makes the template/controller contract implicit (template assumes a `members` property will appear later via side-effect), which is fragile compared to the prior explicit `afterModel`/`setupController` wiring.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test bug: remove_member automatic-group spec uses xhr :put but the route is delete, so the 422 assertion passes by hitting add_members instead and never exercises the real remove_member guard

adjudication.rationale: In the spec, `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` targets the `remove_member` controller action explicitly; in controller specs this bypasses routing, so it does not “hit add_members instead” due to the routes using DELETE for `/members`. The `remove_member` action itself also doesn’t branch on HTTP verb, so using PUT would still exercise the same automatic-group guard (`return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blank-line/re-indentation noise mixed with behavioral changes in this PR obscures the real changes and hampers bisecting, blame, and review; whitespace-only changes belong in separate commits

adjudication.rationale: The diff mixes substantial behavioral changes (e.g., new group pagination/actions in `admin-group.js.es6`, new members API shape in `GroupsController#members`, new admin add/remove member endpoints/routes) with numerous whitespace/format-only changes and re-indentation (e.g., `admin-group-selector.hbs` removing blank lines, indentation-only changes in `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs`, extra blank lines/reindent in `admin/groups_controller.rb`, YAML string-only/format tweaks). This kind of noise makes review/blame/bisect harder and is reasonably actionable as a request to separate formatting-only changes into distinct commits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 mixes this.get("model") access with proxied this.get("limit") style in an ObjectController, which is confusing and will bite during ObjectController deprecation migration

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the controller is an `Em.ObjectController` (which proxies unknown properties to `model`). The diff adds computed properties like `currentPage`/`totalPages` using proxied access (`this.get("user_count")`, `this.get("limit")`, `this.get("offset")`), while the new pagination actions explicitly fetch the model (`var group = this.get("model")`) and then use `group.get("offset")`/`group.get("limit")`. This inconsistency is real and diff-grounded, and could complicate later migration away from ObjectController/proxy semantics, but it does not introduce a concrete runtime defect in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: the offset clamp in findMembers is overwritten by result.meta.offset from the server, so the local clamp either never matters or masks disagreement about who owns clamping

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the clamped `offset` is used in the outgoing AJAX request (`data: { limit, offset }`), so it does affect behavior by preventing negative/out-of-range offsets from being sent. Although `offset` is later set from `result.meta.offset`, that does not make the initial clamp “dead code”; it’s request validation. The diff doesn’t show that the clamp is overwritten before being used or that it never matters.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member return only success_json with no response payload, forcing the client to double-fetch via findMembers to learn the new state

adjudication.rationale: Verified in the diff: Admin::GroupsController#add_members and #remove_member both render only `success_json` (no updated members/meta payload). On the client, Discourse.Group#addMembers and #removeMember explicitly call `self.findMembers()` in their `.then(...)` handlers, which triggers a second request to `/groups/:name/members.json` to refresh state. This is an efficiency/architecture concern (extra round trip), not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently ignores non-existent usernames and still returns success_json, so admin UI shows green even if zero users existed; frontend addMembers also has no .fail() handler

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the loop `usernames.split(",").each` only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` succeeds; non-existent usernames are silently skipped, and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if no users were added). On the frontend, `actions.addMembers` calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without handling the returned promise/rejections (no `.catch`/error path). However, the claim that the “admin UI shows green even if zero users existed” isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (no shown success notification tied to `addMembers`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: removeMember sends user_id in DELETE request body which Rack/Rails may not parse, so params.require(:user_id) can raise and removal silently fails; should send id in query string

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the client sending `DELETE` to `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` with `data: { user_id: ... }` and the server action `remove_member` doing `params.require(:user_id)`. But nothing in the diff demonstrates that Rails/Rack will fail to parse `user_id` for a DELETE with form-encoded data; Rails commonly parses request parameters for DELETE/PUT/PATCH as well as query params. Also, if `user_id` were missing, `params.require(:user_id)` would raise (likely yielding an error response), not “silently” fail as the finding claims. So the asserted defect isn’t verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.delete(user_id) passes an integer where an AR record is required, and group.users.delete persists immediately making the following group.save/render_json_error dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`. The association `delete` call will perform the removal immediately on the association/join table; the subsequent `group.save` does not participate in persisting that removal and is therefore redundant, and the `render_json_error` branch is effectively unlikely to ever run (the group wasn’t modified). However, the claim that passing an integer is invalid can’t be verified from the diff alone (Rails associations often accept ids as well as records).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination math wrong at boundaries: totalPages = floor(user_count/limit)+1 adds an extra empty page when user_count % limit == 0, and next clamps offset to min(offset+limit, user_count) instead of (totalPages-1)*limit, causing unreachable/looping blank pages

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count>0`), which yields an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 50/50 => 2 instead of 1). Additionally, `next` clamps `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, which can set `offset == user_count` (e.g. 50), and `Group.findMembers` then requests `offset: 50` (allowed by its `min(user_count, ...)`), producing an empty members list from `GroupsController#members` (`limit(...).offset(50)` on total 50). This matches the finding: a blank/extra page at boundaries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded limit param on public /groups/:id/members allows any user to request limit=1000000 and serialize entire membership (DoS/data-scraping vector); needs a max clamp

adjudication.rationale: In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the new code sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and applies it directly to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound. This makes the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint accept arbitrarily large `limit` values, enabling very large responses (DoS/data scraping). The finding is directly supported by the diff since no clamp/max is introduced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec uses xhr :put for remove_member but the route is delete, so the spec raises RoutingError instead of asserting the 422

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb under context ".remove_member", the first test calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` but config/routes.rb defines `remove_member` on `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (while PUT is mapped to `add_members`). This makes the test use an HTTP verb that won’t hit the real route, so it doesn’t accurately exercise the routed behavior. However, in a Rails controller spec `xhr :put, :remove_member` generally invokes the action directly (so it’s not verifiable from the diff that it would raise a RoutingError), making the “raises RoutingError” part of the finding unsupported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members is non-transactional: partial failure leaves partial state since group.add calls may have already created GroupUser rows before group.save fails

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, multiple `group.add(user)` calls are performed in a loop before a single `group.save` (no explicit DB transaction):
```rb
usernames.split(",").each { |u| group.add(user) }
if group.save ...
```
The finding’s specific claim that `group.add` has already persisted `GroupUser` rows before `group.save` fails is not verifiable from this diff (the behavior of `Group#add` isn’t shown). However, the lack of a transaction around a multi-step membership update is a real diff-grounded robustness concern: if any step raises or `save` can fail, the operation may not be atomic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unhandled promise/race in member list updates: model.findMembers() return value discarded so transitions don't wait, and rapid next/previous clicks fire overlapping requests where last-arriving response wins

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `afterModel` and now calls `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` for both admin and public routes without returning/awaiting the promise (`admin_group_route.js`, `group-members.js.es6`), so route transitions won’t wait for members to load. More importantly, the new pagination actions (`next`/`previous` in `admin-group.js.es6`) can trigger multiple overlapping `group.findMembers()` AJAX calls with no in-flight guard/cancellation; `findMembers` blindly `setProperties` from whichever response resolves last (`group.js`), so rapid clicks can display stale/incorrect page data depending on response order.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, causing TypeError for callers chaining .then(); should return Ember.RSVP.resolve()

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, the early return was changed from `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to `return ;` when `name` is empty, making the method sometimes return `undefined` instead of a promise. While the diff also removes the in-diff callers that chained `.then(...)` (the `afterModel` hooks), this is still a concrete, diff-grounded contract/edge-case issue: any caller expecting a promise from `findMembers` could break if invoked with an empty name.

adjudication_records.issue_text: External API break: update/create no longer accept the nested group param wrapper; existing API consumers sending group: {...} get fields silently ignored while request still returns 200

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController`, both `create` and `update` were changed to read top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) instead of the previous nested wrapper (`params[:group]...`). There is no backward-compatible fallback to `params[:group]`. In particular, `update` now ignores `params[:group]` entirely and can still `group.save` and return `success_json` (HTTP 200) even if the caller sent only `group: { ... }`, meaning existing clients would see a successful response while their submitted fields are not applied.
